name: Hard-to-vary explanations + Occam's razor
rule: Prefer explanations where every part does work and fewer assumptions are needed. An explanation that fits any outcome explains nothing.
plain: A good explanation would break if you changed its details. A vague one bends to fit anything, so it predicts nothing.

story.beat: Two explanations circulate in the Habitat Ring. One: 'the dome is unlucky; the soil is tired.' Two: 'the new LED batch has drifted toward blue, which stresses this crop and lets blight in.' The first fits any outcome. The second names a batch, a wavelength and a crop, and predicts that the old-batch racks are fine. They are.

examples.text: 'Gremlins' explain every outage. A 'thermal fuse rated too low' explains exactly the afternoon outages, and nothing else.
Two diagnoses fit the symptoms. One needs a single cause; the other needs three rare coincidences. Test the single cause first.
A councillor blames 'bad morale' for everything. When an explanation can't be wrong, it can't guide action either.

realCase.title: Epicycles
realCase.text: Ptolemy's Earth-centred astronomy could fit any new planetary observation by adding another circle on a circle. It was endlessly adjustable, so it explained little. Kepler's ellipses (1609) were hard to vary: change one parameter and the predictions visibly break.

misuse: Using Occam's razor to reject a true but messy cause. Reality is sometimes complicated, and simplest-first is a search order, not a verdict.
sources: David Deutsch, The Beginning of Infinity (2011), ch. 1

predict.prompt: Which explanation is better? A: 'The dome is unlucky.' B: 'LED batch 7 drifted blue and stresses lettuce.'
options: B, because it makes specific predictions that could fail
predict.why: Simple in words isn't the same as good. B is hard to vary and testable.

mcq.prompt: An explanation that fits every possible outcome is…
mcq.why: If nothing could contradict it, it tells you nothing.

whichModel.prompt: A horoscope's 'you may face challenges this week' is true whatever happens.
whichModel.why: It's easy to vary, so it's not a real explanation.
